items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Clear CTE names (top_words, top_synsets) and consistent indentation. Minuses: inconsistent naming (`sense_cnt` vs `top_synset_sense_count`, `word_id` vs `wordid`), trailing whitespace, and a `candidates` CTE whose purpose isn't obvious since it repeats the HAVING filter.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Logic is repeated: `candidates` (`HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2`) duplicates `total_senses >= 2`, and the ORDER BY/LIMIT 500 block appears twice (in top_words and at the end). Changing the sort order means editing two places.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: A single read-only SELECT with no error paths. The constants (2, 500) come from the original query. Data-dependence risks are graded under C8-03-CASE1.

items.name: Semantically equivalent, not just equal on this data
items.name_zh: 语义等价而非仅在当前数据上相等
items.evidence: Ties are broken correctly (COUNT DESC, synsetid ASC; wordid ASC). But words is joined only after LIMIT 500, so it assumes every senses.wordid exists in words and words.wordid is unique. The schema guarantees neither. Orphan senses would return fewer than 500 rows, and duplicate words rows would change counts.
